analysis:
Only CHANGELOG.md head text was supplied (units 11 and 12, lines 233-598). There was no patch hunk and no code diff, so I could not tell which lines are new, and I found no concrete security regression in the changelog prose alone. The entries describe behavior in other files that I did not see, so nothing is verified. Items the next pass should check against source:
(1) Frozen legacy MDM cohort and /v1/enroll gating (lines 250-259): proof freshness, token binding, cohort immutability, and the macOS 27 plus qualified App Attest base-reward requirement. Relevant: TB-009, TB-011, T-036, T-052..T-055, T-057. The changelog admits that generic profiles stay copyable and can enroll directly in MicroMDM.
(2) Persisted cache-routing holder state across restarts (lines 424-428): the stored data and the restore binding to live provider capabilities. Relevant: T-041, TB-007, ADV-001. This persisted store may be a new attack and privacy surface not yet in the threat model. Check holder poisoning and cross-tenant prefix-cache timing, and whether revoked or untrusted providers' holders can be restored.
(3) The SSD cache write-budget raise from 150 to 750 GB/day (line 465) and the TTL raise to 30 minutes (line 547, recorded as the SEC-035 re-acceptance). Relevant: T-016, T-041.
(4) Removal of the GET /v1/provider/earnings and telemetry routes (lines 522-523), and fail-closed attestation challenges (line 524). Relevant: T-031, TB-009. These look like security improvements.
(5) Prompt normalization v8 and renderer identity v4 (line 303), which invalidates cache identities across provider and coordinator.
(6) Billing: cached-prompt pricing with cache-read discounts and settlement refunds (lines 499-505), and the bounded non-streaming response retention (line 373). Relevant: T-007, A-009.
(7) The advisory PR-review workflow's spending and state-writer controls (lines 283-287).
Coverage is documentation-only, so needs_deeper_review is set.
